ai-company-os.consensusSummary: Two creators map how AI work gets systematized beyond individual operators. Dan Eisler reframes agentic engineering as software-factory workflows that combine engineers, agents, and code; Jiaona Zhang

silicon-valley-girl.bio: Silicon Valley Girl interviews AI and tech leaders and translates what they ship into workflows for knowledge workers, creators, and non-engineers. She covers agents, vibe coding, and day-to-day AI productivity, and runs a free newsletter on tools and career strategy. Worth following if you want practitioner demos with the people building the stack, not just commentary.

indydevdan.bio: Dan Eisler, known as Indie Dev Dan, is a software engineer with over 15 years of experience spanning Flash games, Blizzard, finance systems, and early AI coding with tools like Aider. He teaches agentic engineering through his YouTube channel and agenticengineer.com, with a focus on building AI developer workflows and the systems that build systems. He publishes weekly build-and-think content rather than news farming, aimed at engineers who want practical advantage in the age of agents.

aakash-gupta.bio: Aakash Gupta hosts a product growth podcast and newsletter focused on AI-native product work, company operating systems, and how PMs actually ship. He interviews operators building at the frontier and packages the systems they use into concrete playbooks. Worth following if you want operator-level detail on AI tooling, PM craft, and org design rather than hype.

videos.title: Head of ChatGPT & Codex: agents for normal people are HERE
videos.keyTakeaway: OpenAI’s head of ChatGPT and Codex says agents are finally reliable enough that non-technical knowledge workers will get the same leverage early adopters spent two years earning—within months, not years.
videos.executiveSummary: Silicon Valley Girl interviews Tibo, who runs ChatGPT, Codex, and the APIs at OpenAI, on why agents are crossing from technical early adopters into ordinary knowledge work. The conversation is a live working session as much as a talk: they run Codex against email, calendar, computer use, and a half-built content app while Tibo explains what matured (long-horizon reliability, browser/computer use, 100+ plugins, auto-review safety) and what still needs packaging. It responds to the gap between software engineering’s AI transformation—Google’s 75% AI-written code is the reference point—and everyone else’s still-manual research, inbox, and ops load. Tibo’s through-line is augmentation with humans still on the hook, plus a near-term shift of agent memory and files into the cloud so the same assistant follows you across devices.
videos.summary: Silicon Valley Girl interviews OpenAI’s Tibo (ChatGPT, Codex, APIs) on agents becoming reliable for non-technical knowledge workers within months. They demo live Codex workflows—scheduled research, inbox/calendar agents, computer use, skill creator—while he argues humans stay responsible and prompting skill stops being the main moat.
videos.description: Silicon Valley Girl talks with OpenAI’s Tibo on ChatGPT Codex agents for knowledge workers, auto review, and live workflows.
keyPointTitles: Agents finally work for regular people
Knowledge work shifts in six months
Local files give way to cloud memory
Vibe coding still needs tech for scale
Half of Codex use is non-code
Prompt skill stops being the moat

videos.title: FORGET Loop Engineering. Agentic Engineering is about THIS
videos.keyTakeaway: Stop calling it loop engineering — the real leverage is designing AI developer workflows that combine engineers, agents, and code into software factories.
videos.executiveSummary: Dan Eisler (Indie Dev Dan) pushes back on the rising phrase “loop engineering,” which he treats as a hype-filled rebrand of the software development life cycle pushed in circles around figures like Boris Cherny and Peter Steinberger. Drawing on 15+ years as an engineer and years of weekly agentic-engineering content, he reframes the problem as building AI developer workflows inside a software factory: props in, a workflow of code plus agents runs, results out. The video walks from a simple engineer–LLM–review loop up through linters, tests, work trees, sandboxes, kanban intake, specialized hotfix pipelines, and full multi-workflow software factories. His core claim is that value comes from placing three actors — engineers, agents, and code — in the right spots, with engineers mostly at planning and review while the agentic layer compounds the rest.
videos.summary: Indie Dev Dan argues loop engineering is a shallow rebrand of the SDLC and reframes the real work as AI developer workflows that combine engineers, agents, and code. He scales from simple lint loops to sandboxed software factories and specialized paths like production hotfixes, with practical rules: keep it simple, separate code from skills, and design workflows by running them yourself first.
videos.description: Dan Eisler on why loop engineering misses the point—and how AI developer workflows and software factories actually scale agents.
keyPointTitles: Loop engineering is a bad rebrand

videos.title: How to Build a Company OS in Claude Code | Jiaona Zhang | Product Growth
videos.keyTakeaway: A company OS works by encoding the 1% AI-pilled operators' skills into shared GitHub skill files and surfacing them just-in-time in Slack so the other 90–99% know what to use when.
videos.executiveSummary: Aakash Gupta sits down with Jiaona Zhang (Jay-Z), CPO at Laurel and PM instructor at Stanford, formerly CPO at Linktree and a product leader at Airbnb, Webflow, Dropbox, and WeWork. She screen-shares Laurel's full company operating system: a GitHub repo organized by every function, with skill files for each repeatable activity, loaded into Claude and delivered through daily briefings and Slack. The conversation is a practical build guide for teams stuck between a few highly AI-pilled ICs and an org that does not know what to automate. Zhang walks through how to start from one tedious workflow, graduate to playbooks and agents, run non-engineers shipping front-end and back-end features with Devin, and hire for AI maturity by making candidates screen-share how they actually work.
videos.summary: Jiaona Zhang shows Aakash Gupta how Laurel runs a GitHub-based company OS—function folders, skill files, ontologies, and Slack delivery—so AI workflows reach the whole org, not just the 1%. She covers the three-step build path, PMs and CS shipping with Devin, captains and two-track reviews, AI ops staffing, and hiring super-senior IC PMs via screen-share interviews.
videos.description: Jiaona Zhang shows Aakash Gupta how Laurel built a Claude company OS, ships with Devin, and hires AI-pilled IC PMs.
keyPointTitles: AI ops as the new biz ops
